short: California: giant surf and king tides
title: California giant surf and king tides, live: the coast cam by cam
metaTitle: California king tides and giant surf live cams: San Francisco, Pacifica, LA, San Diego (November 2026) | Watch This Cam
desc: Watch California’s coast live as king tides near record highs meet big surf: webcams at Pacifica, San Francisco, Monterey, Santa Monica, Venice, Huntington Beach and San Diego, with the official warnings updated live.
lede: Some of the highest tides of the year are lining up with a big swell along the California coast. The US National Weather Service has High Surf Warnings and Coastal Flood Warnings out from the north coast down to San Diego. These are the live cameras along that coast, with the warnings in force right now and the weather at each camera.

facts.t: San Francisco, Point Reyes, the San Francisco Peninsula coast, Monterey Bay and Big Sur: breaking waves of 20 to 30 ft (6 to 9 m). High Surf Warning until midnight Wednesday night.

The San Francisco tide gauge is forecast to reach 8.5 ft (MLLW) at 10:49 am Wednesday, 2.7 ft above normal. Forecasters say this is approaching the highest tide ever recorded there. Coastal Flood Warning from 6 am to 4 pm Wednesday.

San Luis Obispo and central Santa Barbara County beaches, including Pismo Beach and Morro Bay: breaking waves of 15 to 22 ft (5 to 7 m), until noon Thursday. Ventura County beaches: 8 to 15 ft (2 to 5 m).
Malibu and Los Angeles County beaches: breaking waves of 6 to 11 ft (2 to 3 m), with a High Surf Advisory until 9 pm Thursday and extremely high tides of 8.0 to 8.4 ft.

San Diego County: king tides of 7.9 to 8.3 ft are likely to break the all-time records set in late October. Surf builds to 6 to 8 ft from Wednesday afternoon, with sets up to 10 ft on west-facing beaches. Coastal Flood Warning until 1 pm Friday.
North coast (Humboldt, Del Norte, Mendocino): breaking waves up to 25 ft (8 m) on Wednesday, and up to 2 ft of saltwater flooding possible in low areas around Humboldt Bay.

alerts.match: High Surf Warning|High Surf Advisory|Coastal Flood Warning|Coastal Flood Advisory|Coastal Flood Watch

sections.p: The open ocean just south of San Francisco, where the biggest waves are forecast, and the Bay, where the tide is close to its record. Pacifica Pier and Mori Point face straight into the swell.
Inside the same High Surf Warning, which runs down the Big Sur coast.
A lower-level High Surf Advisory here, but the tides are among the highest of the year, so watch the water climb up the beach around the late-morning high tide.
Where forecasters expect the king tides to break the all-time records set in late October, with surf building from Wednesday afternoon.

links: National Weather Service San Francisco Bay Area
safety: This page is not a forecast. If you are on the coast, follow the National Weather Service and stay well back from the water: forecasters warn that waves this size can pull people into the sea from beaches, jetties and rocks. Cameras can drop offline in a storm.

title: Kīlauea, live: watch Hawaii’s volcano, with today’s official update
metaTitle: Kilauea live cams: watch the Hawaii volcano now, with the USGS alert level | Watch This Cam
desc: Live Kilauea webcams from the US Geological Survey, pointed into Halemaʻumaʻu crater, with the official alert level and today’s eruption update pulled live from the Hawaiian Volcano Observatory.
lede: Kīlauea, on the island of Hawaiʻi, has been erupting in bursts: lava fountains for hours at a time, then a pause while the volcano recharges. These are the US Geological Survey’s own cameras around the summit crater. The box below is the observatory’s latest word, so you can tell at a glance whether a fountain is on or how long it may be until the next one.
factsNote: The alert level and the update in the box below come straight from the US Geological Survey each time this page loads.

facts.t: The eruption is in Halemaʻumaʻu, the crater at Kīlauea’s summit, inside Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park.
On 23 November 2026 the observatory reported the eruption paused after the fountaining of episode 57 that morning, with the summit inflating again and another episode likely in the coming weeks.
facts.src: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory daily update, 23 November 2026

facts.t: USGS alert levels run Normal, Advisory, Watch and Warning. The aviation colour codes run green, yellow, orange and red.

sections.p: Most of these are still pictures from US Geological Survey cameras around the crater, updated through the day. After dark, lava shows as an orange glow.

links: National Park Service: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
safety: This page is not an official warning. For safety information follow the US Geological Survey and the National Park Service.

short: California storm: Sierra snow and giant surf
title: California storm, live: Sierra snow and giant surf, cam by cam
metaTitle: California storm live cams: Lake Tahoe and I-80 snow, giant surf (November 2026) | Watch This Cam
desc: Watch the California storm live: webcams on Interstate 80 at Donner Summit, Highway 50, Lake Tahoe, Mammoth and Highway 395, plus the coast where 25 to 35 ft surf is forecast. With the official warnings, updated live.
lede: A Pacific storm is crossing California and Nevada. The US National Weather Service has Winter Storm Warnings out for the Sierra Nevada and High Surf Warnings along much of the coast. These are the live cameras inside it, with the warnings in force right now and the temperature, snow and wind at each camera.
asOf: the morning of Friday 13 November 2026, Pacific time

facts.t: Lake Tahoe area: heavy wet snow, about 12 inches (30 cm) above 7,000 ft and up to 20 inches (50 cm) on the crest west of the lake. Gusts of 70 to 90 mph (113 to 145 km/h) over the ridges. The warning runs from 10 am Friday to 10 am Saturday.
Northern Sierra above 6,000 ft, including Interstate 80 and Highway 50: 6 to 12 inches (15 to 30 cm) of snow, up to 18 inches (45 cm) on the highest peaks. Until 10 am Saturday.
Mono County and Highway 395: 1 to 2 feet (30 to 60 cm) of snow above 7,000 ft, with gusts of 55 to 70 mph (89 to 113 km/h) along the highway.
Southern Sierra above 6,000 ft, including Yosemite outside the valley, Kings Canyon and Sequoia: up to 20 inches (50 cm) of snow. This warning runs until 4 am Tuesday.
San Francisco and the Big Sur coast: breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft (8 to 11 m), with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft (12 to 15 m) at favoured breaks. High Surf Warning from 6 pm Friday to 4 am Sunday.
Far north coast (Del Norte County): breaking waves of 30 to 40 ft (9 to 12 m), from 1 pm Friday to 4 am Sunday. On the Oregon coast, breakers of 30 to 35 ft (9 to 11 m).
facts.src: NWS Eureka, NWS Medford, NWS Portland

alerts.match: Winter Storm|Blizzard|High Surf Warning|High Wind Warning|Coastal Flood Warning|Avalanche|Winter Weather Advisory

sections.p: The main roads over the Sierra, and the lake between them. The road pictures come from Caltrans and refresh every few seconds. Kingvale and Soda Springs are on the climb to Donner Summit on I-80, and Echo Summit is the top of Highway 50.
The east side of the range, where the wind comes down hardest. Conway Summit is the highest point on Highway 395.

Pacifica sits on the open ocean just south of San Francisco, inside the High Surf Warning. Monterey Bay is more sheltered. Further south, Los Angeles and Orange County beaches are under a lower-level High Surf Advisory.
